content: Certainly. 1. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum to avoid interaction. Monitor the patient closely for any adverse effects. 2. Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by decreasing its solubility as gastric pH increases. Separate the administration of antacids and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by at least 4 hours. Monitor the patient closely. 3. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 4. Calcium carbonate and levofloxacin can mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 5. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of levoketoconazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of levothyroxine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 4 hours and monitor the patient closely. 7. Calcium carbonate increases the effects of lily of the valley through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Monitor the patient closely, as the clinical significance is unknown. 8. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of lisdexamfetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 9. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of lisinopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 10. Calcium carbonate and manganese can mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 11. Mannitol decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 12. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of memantine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 13. Calcium carbonate and mesalamine interact through passive renal tubular reabsorption due to increased pH. Salicylate levels may increase at moderate doses and decrease at high doses due to increased renal excretion of unchanged salicylic acid. Monitor the patient closely. 14. Mestranol decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by shifting magnesium from blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 15. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of methscopolamine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 16. Methyclothiazide increases the levels of calcium carbonate by decreasing renal clearance and decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 17. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Consider separating the administration of antacids and extended-release methylphenidate capsules to avoid altering drug release. 18. Methylprednisolone decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Metolazone decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance and increases the levels of calcium carbonate by decreasing renal clearance. Monitor the patient closely for potential alkalosis or hypercalcemia. 20. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of metoprolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 21. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of mexiletine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 22. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of minocycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Separate their administration by 2 hours. 23. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of moexipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 24. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of moxifloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 25. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 26. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of nadolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 27. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of nebivolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 28. Neomycin decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 29. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. Separate the administration of antacids and neratinib by 3 hours. Monitor the patient closely. 30. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of nicardipine and nifedipine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 31. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid this interaction by administering antacids 2 hours before or after nilotinib. Monitor the patient closely. 32. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of nimodipine by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 33. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of nisoldipine through pharmacodynamic antagonism but increases its levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of nitrendipine by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 35. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 36. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 37. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of ofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 38. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of omadacycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Separate their administration by 2 hours. 39. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of oxytetracycline by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Separate their administration by 2 hours. 40. Calcium carbonate may alter the therapeutic response of palopegteriparatide by affecting serum calcium levels. Measure serum calcium more frequently if co-administered, especially after initiating, discontinuing, or adjusting the dose of these drugs. 41. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of pamidronate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 30 minutes and monitor the patient closely. 42. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the effects of pancrelipase through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 43. Paromomycin decreases the levels of magnesium hydroxide by increasing renal clearance and decreases the levels of calcium carbonate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 44. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If necessary, use short-acting antacids instead of PPIs or H2 antagonists, and separate their administration by several hours. 45. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of penbutolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 46. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of penicillamine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 47. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of perindopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 48. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 49. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of pindolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 50. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of polysaccharide iron by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, while polysaccharide iron increases the levels of calcium carbonate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Monitor the patient closely. 51. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the levels of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 53. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of potassium phosphates (IV) by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. 54. Magnesium hydroxide decreases the effects of potassium phosphates (IV) by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 55. Prednisolone and prednisone decrease the levels of calcium carbonate by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 56. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of propranolol through an unspecified interaction mechanism and by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate their administration by 2 hours and monitor the patient closely. 57. Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of quinapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 58. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of quinidine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Elevated quinidine plasma levels may lead to cardiac conduction disturbances. Use caution and monitor the patient closely.
